requirement_text: For first-year and transfer applicants seeking to enroll in fall 2027, Princeton remains test optional. There are no minimum test score requirements for admission.
researcher_notes: This is the CURRENT live policy as of retrieval (2026-08-21) -- the application cycle now open (2026-27, applying now for fall 2027 entry) is test-optional. Do not confuse with the announced future policy for fall 2028 entry (see REQ-2026-08-21-PRI0002), which is NOT yet in effect. Accepted tests when voluntarily submitted: SAT (code 2672) or ACT (code 2588); Princeton uses SAT score choice and the highest ACT composite; does not superscore across paper/digital SAT formats.

requirement_text: Princeton will return to requiring standardized testing for undergraduate admission beginning with the 2027-28 admission cycle. First-year and transfer applicants seeking to enroll in fall 2028 will need to submit either SAT or ACT scores.
limitations: Describes a policy that takes effect for a future admission cycle (fall 2028 entry); not yet operative as of retrieval date. Exempts active-duty military applicants -- see REQ-2026-08-21-PRI0003.
researcher_notes: Princeton Alumni Weekly (paw.princeton.edu, a princeton.edu subdomain), published 2025-10-09, corroborates from https://paw.princeton.edu/article/princeton-admissions-will-again-require-standardized-tests-2027: "In the fall of 2027, Princeton's undergraduate applicants will again be required to submit SAT or ACT scores." This describes the identical 2027-28 admission cycle from the application-year side (applying fall 2027 = enrolling fall 2028) rather than the entry-year side used on the standardized-testing page. Not a conflict -- two year-anchors (application year vs. entry year) describing the same cycle. Decision rationale per the source page: a five-year review of test-optional data found stronger Princeton academic performance among students who submitted scores than those who did not.

requirement_text: Princeton will not require active military personnel to submit standardized test scores, because lack of regular access to testing facilities and other logistical constraints associated with their service may prevent them from testing at times aligned with Princeton's application deadlines. Active members of the military who opt to apply to Princeton without an SAT or ACT score will not be at a disadvantage in our process.
researcher_notes: Standing exception to the general standardized-testing policy for active-duty military applicants. Not explicitly stated whether this exception continues once general testing is required from fall 2028 entry onward, but its stated rationale (deployment/testing-access constraints) is cycle-independent, so it most plausibly persists through the 2027-28 cycle and beyond -- flagged as an inference, not confirmed. Same application deadlines apply to military applicants as standard applicants; no separate deadline schedule found on this page.

requirement_text: If you apply single-choice early action on Nov. 1, you may not apply to an early program at any other private college or university within the United States. You may apply early to any public institution or service academy, as long as the decision is nonbinding. You may apply early to any international institution, as long as the decision is nonbinding. You may apply early to any college or university with a nonbinding rolling admission process.
researcher_notes: Princeton's Single-Choice Early Action (SCEA) is NON-BINDING (unlike Early Decision at peer institutions) but carries an EXCLUSIVITY restriction: applicants may not apply early to any other private US college/university's early program of any kind (ED, ED2, EA, or REA) while applying SCEA to Princeton. Public universities, international institutions, and nonbinding-rolling programs are explicitly exempted. No Early Decision (binding) program exists at Princeton at all -- SCEA and Regular Decision are the only two first-year admission plans. THIS IS A BINDING CONTRACTUAL COMMITMENT, NOT A CHECKABLE ELIGIBILITY FACT: it should not be auto-converted into a structured_rule threshold by a future interpretation pass without human review -- there is no scalar to compare, and getting the exemption list wrong (e.g. treating a restrictive-early program at another private university as permitted) would misinform a student about a real contractual/honor-code obligation, not just an eligibility estimate.

requirement_text: If English is not your native language and you are attending a school where English is not the language of instruction, you must take the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL), the International English Language Testing System Academic (IELTS Academic), the Duolingo English Test (DET) or the Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic). You are not required to take the TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or PTE Academic if English is your native language or if you have spent at least three years at a secondary school where English is the primary language of instruction.
limitations: Princeton does not publish a minimum passing score for TOEFL/IELTS/DET/PTE on any official admissions or international-student page found in this pass. Third-party test-prep sites (e.g. toeflmocktests.com) publish an unsourced claimed minimum of 'TOEFL 100 iBT' -- this figure appears on no princeton.edu page found here and was deliberately NOT recorded; treat any such figure encountered elsewhere as unverified/unofficial.
researcher_notes: A search snippet (not independently confirmed via direct verbatim fetch) suggested Duolingo (DET) was a recent addition to the accepted-test list 'beginning this admission cycle' -- plausible but not confirmed to a specific cycle year, so not recorded as its own dated fact. test_scale left null because no threshold is published for any of the four accepted tests -- there is no scale/version to qualify without a number attached.

requirement_text: Princeton admission is need-blind -- there is no disadvantage in the admission process for financial aid applicants.
researcher_notes: Statement appears on the international-students page but is phrased as a general policy, not qualified to domestic-only. Corroborated in substance (though not verbatim, via search-engine indexed content rather than a direct fetch) by finaid.princeton.edu describing need-blind admission as covering 'all admission applicants including international students.' This is an institutional policy fact rather than something an applicant submits -- included because it materially affects whether/how a student should apply, which is central to ORYN's Requirement Check and financial-planning use cases.

requirement_text: The full need of all admitted international students is met the same as it is for students from the United States.
researcher_notes: Direct answer to whether Princeton's need-blind/full-need policy extends to international applicants: yes, explicitly, per Princeton's own international-applicants page. This is a more generous policy than most peer institutions, many of which are need-aware or cap aid for international admits.

requirement_text: Students who qualify for financial aid will receive a grant, rather than a loan that has to be repaid.
researcher_notes: Search-engine indexed finaid.princeton.edu content (not independently re-confirmed via a clean direct fetch -- a direct fetch of finaid.princeton.edu/how-aid-works/types-aid returned general aid-types content without this specific sentence) additionally claims: grants have met 100% of demonstrated need since 2001, Princeton was the first US university to eliminate loans from aid packages, and about 83% of recent seniors graduated debt-free. Those three figures are NOT included in requirement_text and are noted here only as unverified-by-direct-fetch context, not as confirmed facts.

requirement_text: Princeton does not offer academic or athletic merit scholarships.
researcher_notes: All Princeton aid is need-based; there is no merit-scholarship pathway to distinguish from the need-based aid deadlines recorded separately.

requirement_text: Princeton does not utilize IDOC, the CSS Profile, or any other College Board documents.
researcher_notes: IMPORTANT for ORYN's deadline records: unlike most peer institutions, Princeton has NO CSS Profile deadline to track. Its financial-aid-application equivalent is its own Princeton Financial Aid Application (PFAA), used by domestic AND international applicants alike, plus FAFSA (US-eligible applicants only) and tax documentation. See deadline records DL-2026-08-21-PRI0005, PRI0006 (PFAA) and PRI0007, PRI0008 (FAFSA) for the actual dates.

requirement_text: Four years of English (including continued practice in writing); four years of mathematics (including calculus for students interested in engineering); four years of one language; at least two years of laboratory science (including physics and chemistry for students interested in engineering); at least two years of history.
limitations: Princeton's own page explicitly states 'This is not a list of admission requirements' regarding this coursework guidance -- it is recommended preparation, not a formal prerequisite. The page separately states: 'we give full consideration to students who don't have access to all of these courses.' Do not surface to students as a hard eligibility gate.
researcher_notes: Engineering-track applicants specifically: calculus and physics+chemistry are called out within this non-mandatory list. Study of visual/performing arts is described as 'typical among applicants' but is not even listed among the recommended coursework items.

requirement_text: Graded Written Paper -- required, preferably in the subjects of English or history.
researcher_notes: Distinctive Princeton-specific requirement, uncommon among peer institutions: applicants submit a piece of graded analytical/expository writing from a high school course, ideally English or history, alongside the standard essay/supplement. This is a required item, not optional.

requirement_text: All applicants must submit the Princeton-specific Questions through the Common Application, in addition to the Common Application itself (CEEB code 2672).
researcher_notes: Checklist page names only the Common Application as the accepted platform (no Coalition Application or QuestBridge application mentioned for first-year applicants on this page). Application fee waiver available via school counselor approval, or institutional waivers from Princeton, ACT, College Board, or NACAC.

requirement_text: School counselor recommendation (School Report) and two teacher recommendations, from two teachers who have taught you in higher level courses, in different academic areas (English, language, humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, or math).
researcher_notes: Counselor recommendation is submitted separately from the School Report (SR) form, though both are typically requested from the same school official. A Midyear School Report is also required once midyear/first-semester senior grades are available -- no fixed calendar date given; tied to each applicant's own school's grading calendar rather than a Princeton-set date.

requirement_text: Optional alumni interviews. Applicants may opt out without disadvantage. Princeton cannot guarantee that every applicant will receive an interview.
researcher_notes: Interviews are alumni-conducted, optional, and availability-limited by geography -- not something an applicant can guarantee or should treat as a required checklist item.
